findings.evidence: Lines 126-132: `rw [Affine.nonsingular_iff] at h`, `rw [Affine.equation_iff] at h1`, then the `simp only [model_a₁, mul_zero, zero_mul, add_zero, model_a₃, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true, zero_pow, ...]` list, which is the shape of `simp?` output.
findings.fix: Replace it with robust automation, e.g. `simp [Affine.nonsingular_iff, Affine.equation_iff] at h` followed by `simp_all`/`grind`, keeping only the model-specific lemmas (`model_a₁` ... `model_a₆`) if `simp` needs them.
findings.issue: `x_ne_zero_of_nonsingular_zero` closes its goal with a 16-lemma squeezed `simp only` (`OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero`, `not_false_eq_true`, `not_true_eq_false`, `pow_eq_zero_iff`, `false_or`, ...) after two named `rw`s. This is a brittle rewrite chain that breaks on any Mathlib rename.

findings.evidence: Examples/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Montgomery/Ladder/Double.lean lines 41 (`coordinates_ne_zero hB`) and 50 (`coordinates_ne_zero (by decide) (k • P)` over `ZMod 2`), both over fields.
findings.fix: Make it public (an unprimed field-level name next to `coordinates_ne_zero`) and use it in the field examples instead of `coordinates_ne_zero hB` / `coordinates_ne_zero (by decide)`.
findings.issue: `coordinates_ne_zero_of_field` is a reusable fact (over a field the coordinate pair is nonzero for every B) but is `private`, so field-level callers still prove `B ≠ 0` to use `coordinates_ne_zero`.

summary: The new B = 0 case rests on a long squeezed `simp only` chain that is fragile under Mathlib renames. A reusable field-level nonvanishing lemma is hidden as private while callers over a field still prove B ≠ 0 by hand.
